status_summary: Executive Order 14186, The Iron Dome for America (signed 2025-01-27, 90 FR 8767), later called Golden Dome, ordered the Defense Secretary to produce within 60 days an architecture covering defense against ballistic, hypersonic and advanced cruise missiles from peer, near-peer and rogue adversaries, accelerated space tracking sensors, proliferated space-based interceptors for boost-phase intercept, underlayer and terminal defenses and non-kinetic capabilities. Executive Order 14369 (signed 2025-12-18) later set a 2028 date for demonstrating next-generation missile defense prototypes and required a report on air and missile defense industrial gaps within 90 days. Congress provided 24.4 billion dollars in the July 2025 reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21, Sec. 20003, integrated air and missile defense), including 5.6 billion for space-based and boost-phase intercept, 7.2 billion for space-based sensors and 250 million for directed energy (per CRS); the program director said about 90 percent was obligated by mid-August 2026. The FY2026 NDAA (P.L. 119-60) aligns national missile defense policy with Golden Dome policy (Sec. 1651) and, per CRS, requires an annual Golden Dome report (Sec. 1652). Northern Command set up Joint Task Force-Gold on 2026-01-15, the director has testified to a 185 billion dollar cost through 2035, and in July 2026 the Space Development Agency awarded 1.75 billion dollars for 36 tracking satellites. The older programs the Mandate names have lagged: in June 2025 Defense News reported the Next Generation Interceptor (NGI) about 18 months behind schedule and the Glide Phase Interceptor about three years behind, with no purchase quantity for NGI given; no quantity of 64 was found. The FY2027 request is 17.5 billion dollars for a Golden Dome fund per CRS (17.9 billion per Aerospace America), with 17.1 billion sought through a reconciliation bill, and Air & Space Forces Magazine reported in October 2026 that Golden Dome has no FY2026 appropriation, so it has no baseline under the continuing resolution that began 2026-10-01; the program director warned in August 2026 that without FY2027 funding there would be no Golden Dome. Homeland cruise missile defense funding and the Mandate's call to keep homeland missile defense out of arms control talks were not verified.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14186, The Iron Dome for America (signed 2025-01-27, published 2025-02-03 at 90 FR 8767), orders a reference architecture and implementation plan within 60 days covering defense against ballistic, hypersonic and advanced cruise missiles from peer, near-peer and rogue adversaries, accelerated space tracking sensors, proliferated space-based interceptors for boost-phase intercept, and underlayer and terminal defenses.

The reconciliation law P.L. 119-21 is enacted; its Sec. 20003 is titled Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for integrated air and missile defense. CRS reports 24.4 billion dollars available until 2029-09-30, including 5.6 billion for space-based and boost-phase intercept, 7.2 billion for military space-based sensors, 250 million for directed energy and 5.9 billion for layered homeland defense; the program director later said about 90 percent was obligated by mid-August 2026.
timeline.source: GovInfo (Public Law 119-21); CRS IN12576; Air & Space Forces Magazine

timeline.event: Executive Order 14369, Ensuring American Space Superiority (published 2025-12-23 at 90 FR 60537), calls for next-generation missile defense prototypes to be developed and demonstrated by 2028, tied to Executive Order 14186, and a report within 90 days on technology, supply chain and industrial gaps for air and missile defense. The text does not mention Golden Dome, space-based interceptors or directed energy by name.

The FY2026 NDAA becomes law as P.L. 119-60; its table of contents lists Sec. 1651 (modification to national missile defense policy to reflect Golden Dome for America policy), Sec. 1652 (Golden Dome missile defense system), Sec. 1653 (technical authority of the Missile Defense Agency Director for integrated air and missile defense) and Sec. 1654 (prohibition on privatized or subscription-based intercept capabilities). CRS says Sec. 1652 requires an annual report covering threat assessment, architecture, and cost and schedule estimates; section text not read.
U.S. Northern Command establishes Joint Task Force-Gold for Golden Dome, led by an Army lieutenant general and co-located at Peterson Space Force Base (per CRS IF13264).

The FY2027 budget materials are released; Aerospace America reports a 17.9 billion dollar Golden Dome request, about 17.1 billion of it through a planned reconciliation package, while CRS (IF13264) gives 17.5 billion for a Golden Dome for America Fund with 17.1 billion requested as mandatory funding; officials acknowledged Congress may not approve the reconciliation part.
Space Development Agency awards 1.75 billion dollars to L3Harris and Sierra Space for 36 missile-tracking satellites in Tranche 3, with launches possible in late 2028.

Program director Gen. Guetlein warns of a funding shortfall for FY2027. He cites a June 2026 test at White Sands, groundbreaking at the first operational site in Virginia, and a Space Force prize competition for space-based interceptors aiming at initial capability by 2028.

At a Senate Armed Services strategic forces subcommittee hearing, the Golden Dome director describes the funding gap; Air & Space Forces Magazine (2026-10-02) reports that Golden Dome has no FY2026 appropriation and so no baseline under the continuing resolution that began 2026-10-01, a Pentagon cost estimate of 185 billion dollars, and an FY2027 request of 17 billion via reconciliation plus 400 million in the base budget, and that senators of both parties urged a bipartisan funding path.
